stem: For an adolescent with frequent daytime symptoms on most days and waking overnight more than once a week, what is a recommended initial treatment?

options.text: Short-acting beta agonist (SABA) alone as needed
Medium to high dose inhaled corticosteroids plus as-needed SABA

explanation: Medium to high dose inhaled corticosteroids plus as-needed SABA is the recommended initial treatment for an adolescent with frequent daytime symptoms and nocturnal waking.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because SABA alone is only appropriate for very infrequent symptoms and does not provide adequate preventer therapy for this level of asthma control.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because frequent daytime symptoms and waking overnight more than once a week indicate poorly controlled asthma that needs a higher starting dose of inhaled corticosteroid therapy with reliever medication as needed.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because montelukast alone is generally insufficient for frequent symptoms and is not the preferred initial treatment here.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because oral prednisolone is used for short courses during acute exacerbations, not as routine long-term initial management.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because low-dose inhaled corticosteroids are unlikely to be enough for an adolescent with symptoms on most days and nocturnal waking.

source.hint: High-frequency symptoms in teenagers require a higher starting tier of inhaled preventer therapy.
